Ministry of MSME Concludes ‘Swachhata Hi Seva 2026’ Campaign with Nationwide Cleanliness and Awareness Initiatives
articles.full_content:
Union Minister for MSME Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi Leads Cleanliness Drive as Ministry of MSME Promotes Jan Bhagidari and Environmental Sustainability under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) observed Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 from 17 th September to 2 nd October 2026, culminating in Swachh Bharat Diwas on 2 October 2026. Guided by the theme “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat”, the campaign focused on promoting cleanliness, environmental sustainability and Jan Bhagidari across the Ministry, its attached offices and autonomous bodies.
As part of the campaign, Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi, Union Minister for MSME; Shri Bharat Khera, Secretary, Ministry of MSME; and Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner (MSME), participated in a cleanliness drive at MSME-DFO, Bal Sahyog, Connaught Place, under the ‘Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath’ initiative on 1 st October 2026. More than 150 participants participated in the cleanliness drive, underscoring the importance of collective action in maintaining clean public spaces. Tree plantation activities were also undertaken under the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ initiative, reinforcing the Ministry’s commitment to environmental conservation and sustainable development.
The campaign commenced with the administration of the Swachhata Pledge by Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner (MSME). Approximately 250 officials of the Ministry of MSME and its field offices participated in the pledge and reaffirmed their commitment to cleanliness and the vision of Swachh Bharat.
As part of awareness and sensitisation activities, the Ministry sensitised officers and representatives of its attached offices, autonomous bodies and field formations on the objectives and significance of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026. The campaign encouraged participating organisations to undertake meaningful cleanliness drives, awareness programmes and sustainable initiatives in their offices and surrounding areas.
During the campaign period, the Ministry and its field formations across the country undertook activities under key components including CTU (Cleanliness Target Unit) Transformation & Clean Public Places, Swachh Paathshala, SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir, Jan Bhagidari for Swachhata, and Swachhata se Samriddhi. These initiatives helped strengthen public participation, promote awareness on cleanliness and reinforce the importance of sustainable and collective efforts towards a Swachh Bharat.

CAQM Reviews Stubble Burning Prevention Measures with District Administrations of Amritsar and Tarn Taran; Conducts Field Visits to Hotspot Villages
articles.full_content:
A high-level team of Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), under the chairmanship of Dr. S.D. Attri, Member (Technical), CAQM, visited Amritsar and Tarn Taran Districts of Punjab, during the ongoing paddy harvesting season. These districts have been identified as hotspots for paddy stubble burning. Apart from field visits, the visiting team held a review meeting in Amritsar today (10.10.2026) with Deputy Commissioners (DCs) and other district-level officials of Amritsar and Tarn Taran district. This visit, apart from deployment of Flying Squads, is in line with high priority attached by the Commission towards achieving the objective of reduction and elimination of paddy stubble burning, a major cause of winter air pollution in NCR and adjoining areas.
The deliberations focused on reviewing preparedness and coordination among the concerned departments and district administration for effective in-situ and ex-situ utilisation of paddy stubble. The Commission stressed upon the importance of facilitating the farmers in terms of timely availability of CRM Machines, sensitizing, conducting Information, Education and Communication (IEC) Activities and providing necessary support.
Along with the review meeting, CAQM undertook field visits on 09.10.2026 and 10.10.2026 to the selected hotspot villages and facilities in districts of Amritsar and Tarn Taran to assess the prevailing ground-level situation and review the implementation of measures aimed at preventing stubble burning.
Regarding the district of Amritsar, the deliberations during the review meeting and field visit included the harvesting and procurement status, along with the availability and deployment of Crop Residue Management (CRM) machinery. It was informed that balers from Amritsar and adjoining districts were operating for collection and management of paddy straw. A supply chain has been established with industries having boilers for utilisation of paddy straw bales, with farmers and aggregators linked to these industries to facilitate ex-situ management. The district has also established a Control Room and Help Desk at the District Administrative Complex to identify farmers requiring CRM machinery and facilitate its availability. A district-level helpline has been circulated for reporting fire and stubble burning incidents to enable prompt action.
Regarding the district of Tarn Taran, the deliberations during the review meeting and field visit included the harvesting and procurement status and the availability and deployment of CRM machinery in the district. It was informed that balers from Tarn Taran and adjoining districts were operating for effective ex-situ management of paddy straw and that the district had substantially achieved its targets regarding procurement and availability of CRM machinery for farmers. These districts have been identified as hotspots for paddy stubble burning.

Minister of State for Coal and Mines inaugurates Third National Conference and Exhibition on Corporate Social Responsibility (NCCSR 2026)
articles.full_content:
Economic progress acquired its fullest meaning when its benefits are reflected in “stronger communities, wider opportunity and more resilient regions”- MoS, Satish Chandra Dubey CSR represented an important expression of the collective effort required for Viksit Bharat: Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Dr. Pallavi Jain Govil
Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, Minister of State, Ministry of Coal and Mines, Government of India, inaugurated the Third National Conference and Exhibition on Corporate Social Responsibility (NCCSR 2026), organised by Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), under Ministry of Corporate Affairs, in New Delhi. The two-day Conference, scheduled on 6–7 October 2026, was organised around the theme “Re-envisioning the Spirit of CSR for Viksit Bharat: From Compliance to Commitment.”
In his Keynote Address, Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, Minister of State for Coal and Mines, emphasised the close relationship between national economic growth, regional development and the well-being of communities in resource-bearing areas. He observed that economic progress acquired its fullest meaning when its benefits were reflected in “stronger communities, wider opportunity and more resilient regions”.
He underlined that, for sectors closely connected with natural resources and local communities, growth and social development could not be viewed as separate objectives. On the occasion, he formally released the Comprehensive CSR Framework for Indian Coal Companies, developed to provide sector-specific direction for more structured, need-based and outcome-oriented CSR interventions in the coal sector.
The inaugural session also witnessed the release of the India CSR Factbook 2024–25, providing a consolidated reference on the evolving CSR landscape in India. The session was graced by Dr. Pallavi Jain Govil , Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India ; Ms. Shoko Ishikawa, UN Women Country Representative in India; Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh , Director General & CEO, IICA ; and Prof. Garima Dadhich , Head, School of Business Environment, IICA .
Delivering the Inaugural Address, Smt. Pallavi Jain Govil , Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs , placed CSR within India’s larger corporate-governance and national-development framework. She stated that the theme of NCCSR 2026 called upon stakeholders to “look beyond the annual obligation” and consider the larger contribution that responsible enterprise could make to India’s development journey. Referring to India’s distinctive statutory CSR architecture, she emphasised that the framework combined statutory obligation with company-level responsibility, Board oversight, public disclosure and impact assessment, and that CSR represented an important expression of the collective effort required for Viksit Bharat . She also released the India CSR Factbook 2024–25 .

articles.title: Third National Conference and Exhibition on Corporate Social Responsibility (NCCSR 2026) concludes, calls for stronger governance, convergence and outcome-oriented CSR for Viksit Bharat
articles.full_content:
CSR is not merely as a statutory obligation but as a strategic instrument for India’s growth: Ajit Seth, former Cabinet Secretary, Govt of India
The Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA) , Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India , concluded the Third National Conference and Exhibition on Corporate Social Responsibility (NCCSR 2026) at The Ashok, New Delhi . The two-day Conference, organised by the School of Business Environment, IICA , was held under the theme “ Re-envisioning the Spirit of CSR for Viksit Bharat: From Compliance to Commitment .”
The Conference concluded with the formal Valedictory Session on “From Compliance to Commitment” , in the presence of Shri Ajit Seth , former Cabinet Secretary, Government of India; Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh , Director General & CEO, IICA; and Prof. Garima Dadhich , Head, School of Business Environment, IICA . The session reviewed the principal issues emerging from the two-day deliberations and reflected on the further strengthening of India’s CSR ecosystem through improved governance, institutional coordination, evidence-based planning and greater emphasis on measurable development outcomes.
Shri Ajit Seth , former Cabinet Secretary, Government of India , in his Valedictory Address, emphasised that the success of Corporate Social Responsibility should not be judged only by the quantum of expenditure, but by the difference it made to people’s lives and to the country’s development. He noted that CSR had emerged as a substantial source of development expenditure and observed that the framework had deliberately placed responsibility with company Boards, thereby embedding CSR within the wider evolution of corporate governance and responsible conduct.
He cautioned against tokenism and underlined the need to scale up effective interventions, address geographical imbalances in CSR spending and extend greater attention to underserved districts. He also stressed that technology could strengthen visibility, monitoring and accountability, but could not substitute field knowledge and administrative judgement. Calling upon companies to view CSR not merely as a statutory obligation but as a strategic instrument for India’s growth , he said that stronger convergence among stakeholders and sustained attention to inclusive and sustainable outcomes would contribute to the broader vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 .
Following the Valedictory Address, Shri Ajit Seth released the Compendium of CSR Best Practices 2025 , which brings together the practices showcased by exhibitors during NCCSR 2025. The publication forms part of IICA’s effort to document and disseminate implementation experiences and replicable CSR practices for wider institutional learning.
